answer.evidence: The silhouette is a lens-shaped heap that widens from 10px at row 6 to 28px at rows 10-11, then narrows to 6px at row 15. The upper rows 6-9 carry the lighter highlights (L about 115-147 in columns x=9, 16 and 22) and read as the heap's sloped upper surface. Rows 10-15 step down to darker values (L about 43-90), which read as the shaded front flank and base, about 5-6 rows tall. There is no hard front-edge line, because the shading grades softly as expected for a loose pile. A heap with a lit top and a shaded front still reads as a volume, not a flat slab.

styleAnswer.evidence: The ash mound is a low, flat grey oval, smaller than one tile, so the per-tile tone count is 0 and I judged density by eye. It has only about 3 visible grey steps: a lighter top, a mid body and a dark rim, plus a few speckle dots. The references (well, hedge, stall) carry about 5-6 steps per material and per-piece highlights. All of its dark edge pixels (100%) are neutral, so the rim reads as a neutral dark line rather than a darker tone of the ash. That is the 'sticker' look. The hedge and well outlines are tinted at 0% and 33% neutral. The bench and lamp references are also small or thin, so size alone is not the issue. Next to them the mound still looks flatter and less shaded, with little grain, no clumps and no individually shaded lumps. Because of the neutral outline and shallow ramp, I would not accept it beside the Beodeul references.
